correctness.rationale: Benoist's inspected full text states the equidegree partial degree \(\binom{N+1}{c}d^{c-1}(d-1)^{N-c+1}\) and the identity that total degree is the sum of partial degrees. The valuation formula follows exactly from \(c\binom{N+1}{c}=(N+1)\binom{N}{c-1}\) and Legendre's factorial valuation, with the binomial valuation equal to the number of binary carries in \((c-1)+(n+1)\). The parity and mod-4 consequences are proved by exhausting the even/odd cases for d symbolically. Exact replay across 204120 parameter triples agrees.

value.rationale: The discriminant degree is the basic projective degree of the singular-member divisor in the parameter space of complete intersections. Benoist's characteristic-2 square phenomenon makes powers of two a geometrically motivated arithmetic question rather than an arbitrary residue exercise. The result gives the full 2-adic valuation for an infinite geometric family from binary carry data, and its sharp corollaries separate the unique odd-degree hypersurface regime from universal four-divisibility in all nonempty higher-codimension equidegree cases.
